facts.statement: The genus Sauropelta was first described by John Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: authority: Ostrom, 1970

facts.statement: Sauropelta lived during the Early Cretaceous Period in North America.
facts.quote: Sauropelta ( ; meaning 'lizard shield') is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur that existed in the Early Cretaceous Period of North America.

facts.statement: Most Sauropelta fossils come from the Cloverly Formation, which dates to 108.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: most of its remains are found in a section of the Cloverly Formation dated to 108.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Sauropelta was a medium-sized dinosaur measuring between 5.2 and 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Sauropelta is a medium-sized nodosaurid, measuring about 5.2 - 6 m long.

facts.statement: Sauropelta possessed a very long tail that constituted approximately half of its total body length.
facts.quote: Sauropelta had a distinctively long tail which made up about half of its body length.

facts.statement: Sauropelta weighed up to 1.5 to 2 metric tons.
facts.quote: weighing up to about 1.5 - 2 MT.

facts.statement: The substantial weight of Sauropelta was primarily due to extensive bony armor and large spines on its neck.
facts.quote: The extra weight was largely due to its extensive covering of bony armor, including the characteristically large spines projecting from its neck.

facts.statement: When viewed from above, the Sauropelta skull was triangular with a wider rear and a tapering snout.
facts.quote: The skull was triangular when viewed from above, with the rear end wider than the tapering snout.

facts.statement: The widest part of a Sauropelta skull, located behind the eyes, measured 35 centimeters.
facts.quote: One skull measured 35 centimeters (13.75 in) in width at its widest point, behind the eyes.

facts.statement: The Sauropelta skull roof was very thick, covered in tightly fused flat bony plates that appeared to lack sutures.
facts.quote: The roof of the skull was very thick and covered in flat, bony plates that are so tightly fused that there appear to be no sutures (boundaries) like the ones seen in Panoplosaurus, Pawpawsaurus, Silvisaurus, and many other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Sauropelta had leaf-shaped teeth in both jaws used for cutting plant material.
facts.quote: More typically for nodosaurids, leaf-shaped teeth lined both upper and lower jaws, used for cutting plant material.

facts.statement: Although the front of the skull is unknown, Sauropelta likely had a sharp bony ridge at the jaw tips to support a keratinous beak.
facts.quote: The front end of the skull is unknown, but there would have been a sharp bony ridge (tomium) at the end of both upper and lower jaws, as seen in other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: One skeleton preserved forty tail vertebrae, suggesting the true count may have exceeded fifty.
facts.quote: One skeleton preserved forty caudal (tail) vertebrae, although some were missing, suggesting that the true number of caudal vertebrae may have exceeded fifty.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons ran along the length of the Sauropelta tail to stiffen it.
facts.quote: Ossified tendons stiffened the tail along its length.

facts.statement: Sauropelta was covered in armor made of bony masses embedded in the skin known as osteoderms.
facts.quote: Like other nodosaurids, Sauropelta was covered in armor formed from bony masses embedded in the skin (osteoderms).

facts.statement: Small bony nodules separated larger conical scutes arranged in side-to-side rows on the Sauropelta back and tail.
facts.quote: On the upper surface of the back and tail, the skin was covered in small, bony nodules (ossicles), which separated larger conical scutes arranged in parallel rows along the mediolateral axis (side to side).

facts.statement: Barnum Brown collected the holotype specimen of Sauropelta from the Cloverly Formation in Big Horn County, Montana, in the early 1930s.
facts.quote: In the early 1930s, famed dinosaur hunter and paleontologist Barnum Brown collected the holotype specimen of Sauropelta (AMNH 3032, a partial skeleton) from the Cloverly Formation in Big Horn County, Montana.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered two additional Sauropelta specimens, AMNH 3035 and AMNH 3036.
facts.quote: Brown also discovered two other specimens (AMNH 3035 and 3036).

facts.statement: John Ostrom led expeditions in the 1960s that recovered additional incomplete Sauropelta specimens from the Cloverly Formation.
facts.quote: Expeditions in the 1960s led by the equally renowned John Ostrom of Yale University's Peabody Museum of Natural History recovered additional incomplete specimens from the Cloverly.

facts.statement: John Ostrom named the genus Sauropelta in 1970 to include remains found by both the Brown and Ostrom expeditions.
facts.quote: In 1970, Ostrom coined the genus Sauropelta to include remains discovered by both expeditions.

facts.statement: The name Sauropelta is derived from Greek words meaning 'lizard' and 'shield', referencing its bony armor.
facts.quote: Derived from the Greek σαυρος () ('lizard') and πελτε () ('shield'), this name is a reference to its bony armor.

facts.statement: The species name was corrected from S. edwardsi to S. edwardsorum in 1991 by George Olshevsky to follow Latin grammar rules.
facts.quote: Although Ostrom originally named the species S. edwardsi, nomenclaturist George Olshevsky corrected the spelling to S. edwardsorum in 1991 to conform to Latin grammar rules.

facts.statement: Confusion arose in 1972 when the name "Peltosaurus" was accidentally published as a photo caption for specimen AMNH 3036.
facts.quote: Despite the naming of Sauropelta two years earlier, confusion arose in 1972 when the name "Peltosaurus" was inadvertently published as the caption of a photograph of AMNH 3036.

facts.statement: The name Peltosaurus is invalid for the dinosaur because it was previously used for a genus of North American lizard.
facts.quote: However, the name Peltosaurus was preoccupied by a genus of North American lizard from an extinct branch of the modern family Anguidae (the alligator lizards and the legless glass lizards) and is no longer used to refer to the dinosaur.

facts.statement: In 1999, Carpenter described nodosaurid material from the Poison Strip Sandstone in Utah, a formation contemporaneous with the Cloverly.
facts.quote: In 1999, Carpenter and colleagues described material of a large nodosaurid from Utah, discovered in a member of the Cedar Mountain Formation called the Poison Strip Sandstone, which is contemporaneous with the Cloverly Formation.

facts.statement: In recent publications, Carpenter no longer assigns the Poison Strip nodosaurid to Sauropelta, classifying it only within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: In more recent publications, Carpenter no longer refers the Poison Strip animal to Sauropelta, only to the family Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Sauropelta is classified as a member of the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Since John Ostrom first described Sauropelta in 1970, it has been recognized as a member of the family Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids, including Sauropelta, belong to the infraorder Ankylosauria along with the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: The nodosaurids, along with the family Ankylosauridae, belong within the infraorder Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids are characterized by a lower jaw that curves downwards at the end.
facts.quote: Nodosaurids are characterized by certain features of the skull, including the mandible (lower jaw), which curves downwards at the end.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids generally had narrower snouts than ankylosaurids and lacked the heavy tail clubs found in ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Overall, nodosaurids had narrower snouts than the ankylosaurids, and also lacked the heavy ankylosaurid tail clubs.

facts.statement: Sauropelta, Silvisaurus, and Pawpawsaurus are sometimes considered basal to younger nodosaurids like Panoplosaurus, Edmontonia, and Animantarx.
facts.quote: While the systematics (evolutionary relationships) of nodosaurids have not been firmly established, the genera Sauropelta, Silvisaurus and Pawpawsaurus are sometimes considered to be basal to geologically younger nodosaurids like Panoplosaurus, Edmontonia, and Animantarx.

facts.statement: Sauropelta remains have been found in the U.S. states of Wyoming, Montana, and possibly Utah.
facts.quote: Anatomically, Sauropelta is one of the most well-understood nodosaurids, with fossilized remains recovered in the U.S. states of Wyoming, Montana, and possibly Utah.

facts.statement: Sauropelta is the earliest known genus of nodosaurine dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It is also the earliest known genus of nodosaurine

facts.statement: Sauropelta was a heavily built quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Sauropelta was a heavily built quadrupedal herbivore

facts.statement: In 1932, Charles Mortram Sternberg reported large four-footed dinosaur footprints from Lower Cretaceous rocks in British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: In 1932, Charles Mortram Sternberg reported the presence of the footprints of a large, four-footed dinosaur from Lower Cretaceous rocks in British Columbia, Canada.

facts.statement: In 1984, Kenneth Carpenter re-examined tracks previously attributed to ceratopsians and argued they were made by ankylosaurs, specifically Sauropelta.
facts.quote: However, in 1984 paleontologist Kenneth Carpenter re-examined the British Columbian Tetrapodosaurus prints and argued that they were made by ankylosaurs rather than ceratopsians.

facts.statement: Large numbers of tracks were discovered at the Smoky River Coal Mine near Grande Cache, Alberta, five years after Carpenter's re-examination.
facts.quote: Five years later, large numbers of Tetrapodosaurus tracks were discovered at the Smoky River Coal Mine near Grande Cache, Alberta.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Sauropelta edwardsorum were found in the Cloverly Formation in Wyoming and Montana, dating to 108.5 million years ago in the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: All specimens of S. edwardsorum were recovered from the Little Sheep Mudstone section of the Cloverly Formation in Wyoming and Montana, which has been dated to 108.5 million years ago, during the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Sauropelta lived in forested plains and browsed on conifers and cycads, as grasses had not yet evolved.
facts.quote: Abundant fossil remains of coniferous trees suggest that these plains were covered in forest. Grasses would not evolve until later in the Cretaceous, so Sauropelta and other Early Cretaceous dinosaurian herbivores browsed from a variety of conifers and cycads.

facts.statement: Sauropelta had a narrow snout, an adaptation for selective browsing rather than grazing.
facts.quote: Nodosaurids like Sauropelta had narrow snouts, an adaptation seen today in animals that are selective browsers as opposed to the wide muzzles of grazers.

facts.statement: Deinonychus was abundant in the Cloverly Formation and fed on herbivores like Sauropelta, evidenced by the large number of its teeth found there.
facts.quote: The dromaeosaurid theropod Deinonychus fed upon some of these herbivores, and the sheer number of Deinonychus teeth scattered throughout the formation are a testament to its abundance.

facts.statement: The apex predator of the Cloverly ecosystem was the large carcharodontosaurid theropod Acrocanthosaurus.
facts.quote: The apex predators of the Cloverly was the large carcharodontosaurid theropod Acrocanthosaurus.

facts.statement: Sauropelta had a hard body armor reinforced by huge spikes, and its defensive tactic involved falling to the ground and digging its feet in to prevent being flipped over.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo estaba provisto de una coraza dura reforzada por enormes espinas que facilitaban su defensa ante los ataques de sus depredadores, su único punto débil era su descubierto abdomen, así pues su táctica defensiva consistía en dejarse caer y clavar sus patas en el suelo para que no lo pudieran voltear.

facts.statement: Sauropelta was a medium-sized nodosaurid measuring about 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Era un nodosáurido de tamaño mediano, midiendo cerca de 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Despite being smaller than a modern black rhinoceros, Sauropelta weighed approximately 1,500 kilograms.
facts.quote: Aunque su cuerpo fuera más pequeño que el de un moderno rinoceronte negro, Sauropelta tenía una masa casi igual, pesando en aproximadamente 1.500 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Much of Sauropelta's weight came from its extensive bony armor, including large spikes projecting upward from its neck.
facts.quote: El peso adicional era en gran parte debido a su extensa armadura ósea, incluyendo las características púas grandes que se proyectaban de su cuello hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The genus Sauropelta was named by Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Ostrom, 1970

facts.statement: The species Sauropelta edwardsorum was named by Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: species_authority: Ostrom, 1970

facts.statement: "Peltosaurus" is a synonym of Sauropelta, proposed by Anónimo in 1972.
facts.quote: synonyms: "Peltosaurus" Anónimo, 1972

facts.statement: Sauropelta edwardsorum is the only known species in the extinct genus Sauropelta.
facts.quote: Sauropelta edwardsorum es la única especie conocida del género extinto Sauropelta

facts.statement: Sauropelta lived during the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 108.5 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 108,5 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Sauropelta's body was equipped with a hard armor reinforced by huge spikes to defend against predator attacks.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo estaba provisto de una coraza dura reforzada por enormes espinas que facilitaban su defensa ante los ataques de sus depredadores

facts.statement: Sauropelta was a heavily built quadrupedal herbivore approximately 5.2 meters long and weighing 1.5 tons.
facts.quote: Sauropelta fue un cuadrúpedo herbívoro pesadamente construido con un cuerpo de aproximadamente 5,2 metros de largo y un peso de 1,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The skull was triangular when viewed from above, with the posterior end wider than the narrow snout.
facts.quote: El cráneo era triangular cuando era visto desde arriba, con el extremo posterior más ancho que el hocico angosto.

facts.statement: A skull measures 35 centimeters across at its widest point behind the eyes.
facts.quote: Un cráneo mide 35 centímetros de lado a lado en su punto más ancho, detrás de los ojos.

facts.statement: Thick triangular shields project from the postorbital bone above and behind the eyes and from the jugal bone below and behind the eyes.
facts.quote: Como en otros dinosaurios, escudos triangulares gruesos se proyectan del postorbital, sobre y detrás de los ojos, así como también del yugal el hueso, debajo y detrás de los ojos.

facts.statement: Leaf-shaped teeth were aligned in the upper and lower jaws and used for grinding plant material.
facts.quote: Los dientes foliformes se alinearon las quijadas superiores e inferiores, siendo usadas para moler el material vegetal.

facts.statement: The tail was characteristically long, nearly half the total length of the animal.
facts.quote: La cola de Sauropelta era caracteristicamente larga, cerca de la mitad del largo total del animal.

facts.statement: A skeleton preserves forty caudal vertebrae, suggesting the true number may have exceeded fifty.
facts.quote: Un esqueleto preserva cuarenta vértebras caudales, aunque algunas faltaran, sugiriendo que el número verdadero de vértebras caudales pudo haber excedido los cincuenta.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons ran along the entire length of the tail.
facts.quote: Tendones osificados atiesaron la cola en todo su recorrido.

facts.statement: Like other nodosaurids, Sauropelta was covered by bony armor strongly embedded in the skin, called osteoderms.
facts.quote: Como otros nodosáuridos, Sauropelta estaba cubierto por una armadura ósea fuertemente incrustada en la piel, los llamados osteodermos.

facts.statement: Two parallel rows of domed shields ran from the dorsal surface of the neck along the back to the tail.
facts.quote: Dos filas del paralelas de escudos abovedados desde la superficie dorsal del cuello por la espalda hasta la cola.

facts.statement: Over the hips, small ossicles and larger domed plates were tightly fused to form a structure called the sacral shield.
facts.quote: Sobre las caderas, los osículos y las placas abovedadas más grandes estaban fjadas muy firmemente para formar una estructura llamada protector sacro.

facts.statement: Extremely large dorsal spines lined the sides of the neck, increasing in size toward the shoulders and then decreasing until they disappeared before the hips.
facts.quote: Las espinas dorsales, extremadamente grandes, sw alinearon los lados del cuello, aumentando de tamaño hacia los hombros, y después disminuyendo de tamaño otra vez a lo largo del lado del cuerpo hasta que desaparecían antes de las caderas.

facts.statement: Behind the hips, flat triangular plates lined the tail on both sides, pointing outward and decreasing in size toward the tail tip.
facts.quote: Detrás de las caderas, las placas triangulares planas alinearon la cola en ambos lados, apuntando hacia fuera y disminuyendo de tamaño hacia el extremo de la cola.

facts.statement: In the early 1930s, paleontologist Barnum Brown collected the holotype specimen AMNH 3032, a partial skeleton, from the Cloverly Formation in Big Horn County, Montana.
facts.quote: A principio de los años de 1930, el famoso cazador de dinosaurios y paleontólogo Barnum Brown recolectó el espécimen holotipo de Sauropelta, AMNH 3032, un esqueleto parcial, de la Formación Cloverly en el Condado de Big Horn, Montana.

facts.statement: Brown also discovered two other specimens, AMNH 3035 and AMNH 3036.
facts.quote: Brown también descubrió otros dos especímenes, AMNH 3035 y AMNH 3036.

facts.statement: The last of these is the best known example of a nodosaurid, including much of the armor in situ, and is exhibited at the American Museum of Natural History in New York.
facts.quote: El último de estos es el mejor ejemplo conocido de un nodosáurido, incluyendo mucho de la armadura in situ, siendo exhibido en el Museo Americano de Historia Natural de Nueva York.

facts.statement: In 1970, Ostrom coined the name Sauropelta to include the remains from both expeditions.
facts.quote: En 1970, Ostrom acuñó el nombre Sauropelta para incluir los restos de ambas expediciones.

facts.statement: The name derives from the ancient Greek sauros, meaning 'lizard', and pelte, meaning 'shield', referring to the armor covering its body.
facts.quote: Este deriva del griego antiguo σαυρος/sauros, "lagarto"y πελτε/pelte, "escudo", haciendo referencia a la armadura que cubría su cuerpo.

facts.statement: Although Ostrom originally named the species S. edwardsi, George Olshevsky corrected the name to S. edwardsorum in 1991 according to Latin grammar.
facts.quote: Aunque Ostrom aoriginalmente llamara a la especie S. edwardsi, en la nomenclatura binomial George Olshevsky corrigió el nombre a S. edwardsorum en 1991 conforme a la gramática latina.

facts.statement: In 1999, Carpenter and colleagues described a nodosaurid from Utah found in the Poison Strip Sandstone, part of the Cedar Mountain Formation, which is contemporaneous with the Cloverly Formation.
facts.quote: En 1999, Carpenter y colegas describieron un nodosáurido proveniente de Utah, descubierto en la Arenisca Poison Strip, parte de la Formación Montaña Cedar, contemporánea a la Formación Cloverly.

facts.statement: In 1984, paleontologist Kenneth Carpenter reexamined the Tetrapodosaurus tracks from British Columbia and argued they were made by ankylosaurians rather than ceratopsians.
facts.quote: En 1984 el paleontólogo Kenneth Carpenter reexaminó las huellas del Tetrapodosaurus de la Columbia Británica y argumentó que fueron hechas por anquilosaurianos en lugar de ceratopsianos.

facts.statement: Specifically, Carpenter concluded that they were likely the tracks of Sauropelta.
facts.quote: Específicamente, Carpenter concluyó que probablemente se trataba de las huellas de Sauropelta.

facts.statement: Five years later, a large number of Tetrapodosaurus tracks were discovered in the Smoky River coal mine near Grande Cache, Alberta.
facts.quote: Cinco años después, un gran número de huellas de Tetrapodosaurus se descubrieron en la mina de carbón Smoky River cerca de Grande Cache, Alberta.

facts.statement: This site is considered the most important ankylosaur track site in the world.
facts.quote: Este sitio es considerado el sitio de rastros de anquilosaurios más importante del mundo.

facts.statement: Since John Ostrom first described Sauropelta in 1970, it has been recognized as a member of the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Desde queJohn Ostrom describiera por primera vez a Sauropelta en 1970, este ha sido reconocido como miembro de la familia Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids, along with the family Ankylosauridae, form the suborder Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: Los nodosáuridos, junto con la familia Ankylosauridae, forman el infraorden Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Nodosaurids are characterized by certain skull features, including a lower jaw with a downward curve at the rostral end.
facts.quote: Los nodosáuridos se caracterizan por ciertas características del cráneo, incluyendo la quijada inferior con una curva descendente en el extremo rostral.

facts.statement: Superficially, nodosaurids possess narrower skulls than ankylosaurids and lack the distinctive club at the tail end.
facts.quote: Superficialmente los nodosáuridos poseen cráneos más estrechos que los de los anquilosaúridos y no poseen la distintiva porra en el extremo de la cola de estos.

facts.statement: Both ankylosaurids and nodosaurids have been found mainly in North America, Asia, and Europe.
facts.quote: Tanto los anquilosáuriodos como los nodosáuridos han sido encontrados principalmente en América del norte, Asia y Europa.

facts.statement: In a 2001 phylogenetic analysis, Carpenter included the three earliest genera in a sister clade to a group containing the last three, though he found Panoplosaurus could belong to any clade depending on which taxa and characters were chosen.
facts.quote: En un análisis filogenético de 2001, Carpenter incluyó los tres géneros primeros en un clado hermano a un grupo que contenía los últimos tres, aunque él encontrara que Panoplosaurus podría pertenecer a cualquier clado, dependiendo que taxones y los caracteres fueran elegidos.

facts.statement: A nodosaurid from Utah discovered in the Poison Strip Sandstone, part of the Cedar Mountain Formation, is contemporaneous with the Cloverly Formation.
facts.quote: En 1999, Carpenter y colegas describieron un nodosáurido proveniente de Utah, descubierto en la Arenisca Poison Strip, parte de la Formación Montaña Cedar, contemporánea a la Formación Cloverly.

facts.statement: The bases of each pair of cervical dorsal spines and each pair of caudal plates were fused together, greatly restricting mobility in the neck and the first part of the tail.
facts.quote: Las bases de cada par de espinas dorsales cervicales y de cada par de placas caudales estaban fundidas juntas, restringiendo mucho movilidad en el cuello y la primera parte de la cola,

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 6 meters and weight at 2 tons, while Thomas Holtz gave a higher estimate of 7.6 meters.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul lo estimó en 6 metros y 2 toneladas. Thomas Holtz dio una estimación más alta de 7,6 metros.

facts.statement: Carpenter originally described the cervical dorsal spines and caudal plates as belonging to a single row on each side, but more recently he and James Kirkland reconstructed them in two parallel rows on each side, one over the other.
facts.quote: Carpenter describió originalmente las espinas dorsales cervicales y las placas caudales como perteneciendo a una sola fila a cada lado, aunque más recientemente él y James Kirkland la ha reconstruido en dos filas paralelas a cada lado, uno sobre la otro.
